title: Standardise text, numbers and typos
concept:
Three regions in the export are typed differently: `" attica "` (spaces, lower case), `"CRETE"` and `"crete"`. Excel's criteria ignore case, so `=COUNTIF(D2:D183,"Crete")` still finds CRETE. But **spaces are characters**: `=COUNTIF(D2:D183,"Attica")` returns **{{=COUNTIF(D2:D183,"Attica")}}** and misses `" attica "`, and a pivot shows it as a separate row.

**Standardise text** with a helper column: `=TRIM(PROPER(D2))`. PROPER sets the first letter of each word to a capital and the rest to lower case; TRIM removes spaces at the ends and doubles in the middle. Fill it down, then **Copy ▸ Paste Special ▸ Values** over column D and delete the helper. (Google Sheets also has Data ▸ Data cleanup ▸ Trim whitespace, which only trims.)

**Numbers stored as text** sit left-aligned with a small green corner. They look like numbers, but SUM, COUNT and pivots skip them: `=SUM(G2:G183)` is **{{=SUM(G2:G183)}}** and `=COUNT(G2:G183)` counts **{{=COUNT(G2:G183)}}** of the 182 quantities. Fix them with the ⚠ icon ▸ **Convert to Number**, or `=VALUE(G2)` in a helper column.

**Typos in IDs** break lookups. One ProductID reads `P0O2`: a letter O where a zero belongs. Its price lookup is #N/A, and wrapped in IFERROR it silently becomes 0. Fix it with **Find & Replace**, scoped to the ProductID column, with *Match entire cell contents* ticked.

> [!warn] Find & Replace hits every cell in its scope. Replace O with 0 across the whole sheet and every OrderID (O1001 …) turns into a number (1001). Scope it, then check the count Excel reports.

**Impossible dates.** The file is for 2025, so a 2026 date is a typing slip. Sort the Date column newest first and it jumps to the top; fix the year.

args.name: text
args.desc: removes spaces at both ends, and repeats in the middle

args.name: text
args.desc: First Letter Capital, the rest lower case

worked.prompt: Standardise O1012's region (row 13, stored as " attica ").
worked.explain: PROPER turns ` attica ` into ` Attica `; TRIM strips the spaces. Result: **{{=TRIM(PROPER(D13))}}**. Filled down column D and pasted as values, the same formula fixes every region at once.

mistakes: TRIM alone: ` attica ` becomes `attica`, still lower case. PROPER alone keeps the spaces. You need both.
Writing `=TRIM(D2)` in D2 itself: a circular reference. Use a helper column, then paste values.
Find & Replace with no scope: `O` → `0` everywhere turns every OrderID into a number.
Leaving numbers stored as text: nothing errors, the totals are just short.

drills.ask: In the formula bar, return **O1076**'s Region (row 78) standardised, using TRIM and PROPER, and press **Test**.
Standardise **every Region** in column D: no stray spaces, a capital first letter. (Blank regions don't count in this drill.) Then press **Check**.

defects.label: O1012 Region has stray spaces and lower case
O1140 Region is in lower case

drills.hint: Formula fill `=TRIM(PROPER(D2))` into column D, every row.

solution.explain: =TRIM(PROPER(D2)) filled down D, pasted as values.

drills.ask: Make every **Quantity** a real number. Then press **Check**.

defects.label: O1045 Quantity is stored as text
O1150 Quantity is stored as text

drills.hint: Look for the green corners in column G, then Convert to Number on G (or fill `=VALUE(G2)` into G).

solution.explain: Convert to Number on column G.

drills.ask: One ProductID has a letter O where a zero belongs. Fix it with **Find & Replace**, without changing anything else. Then press **Check**.

defects.label: O1088 ProductID has a letter O instead of a zero

drills.hint: The bad ID is `P0O2`. Replace it with `P002`, within column C, matching the entire cell.

solution.explain: Find P0O2, replace with P002, within column C, match entire cell contents.

drills.ask: One order is dated **2026**, a year after everything else. Find it and correct the year. Then press **Check**.

defects.label: O1170 is dated 2026: a typo for 2025

drills.hint: Sort by Date, largest first: it's the top row. Keep the day and month; change only the year to 2025.

questions.explain: PROPER fixes the case, TRIM the spaces; you need both. UPPER would give ATTICA.

questions.prompt: A quantity is left-aligned with a green corner. What does SUM do with it?
questions.explain: It's text that looks like a number. SUM, COUNT and pivot sums skip text, so the total is quietly short.

questions.prompt: Find `O`, replace with `0`, **all columns**. What happens to order O1001?
questions.explain: Replace reaches every cell in scope, and Excel re-reads the result: "01001" is a number, so the ID becomes 1001.

claimAfter: I can standardise messy text, fix numbers stored as text, and correct typos safely with Find & Replace.
notYet: You haven't summarised anything yet. Pivot tables come next.
